title: Renderer/action `visible`/`disabled` predicates bypass the canonical CEL engine — home-grown JS evaluator diverges from server enforcement
body:
Found while auditing the client-side blast radius of framework#3183 (the `dateField == today()` silent-miss, fixed in framework#3205).

## The split

ObjectUI evaluates runtime predicates through **two different engines**, and they systematically diverge:

| Path | Sites | Engine | CEL-correct? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **A — field rules** | `visibleWhen` / `readonlyWhen` / `requiredWhen` | `packages/core/src/evaluator/fieldRules.ts` → delegates to `@objectstack/formula`'s `ExpressionEngine.evaluate` | ✅ canonical — same verdict as server enforcement (its header explicitly cites the framework's *"No private expression DSL"* rule) |
| **B — component/action predicates** | `visible` / `hidden` / `disabled` / `visibleOn` / `hiddenOn` / `disabledOn` (`SchemaRenderer.tsx:277-316`), action buttons via `useExpression.ts` / `useCondition`, `ExpressionProvider.tsx` | home-grown `packages/core/src/evaluator/ExpressionEvaluator.ts` — compiles the predicate as **plain JavaScript** (`ExpressionCache.compile` → `fn(...)`) | ❌ not CEL at all |

Path B unwraps a `{ dialect: 'cel', source }` envelope but then **ignores the dialect** and executes the source as JS (`ExpressionEvaluator.evaluate`, comment says "the underlying syntax is identical" — it isn't):

- `FormulaFunctions` has **no** `today` / `daysFromNow` / `daysAgo` / `now` — any date predicate an author writes per the platform's CEL catalog throws `today is not defined` → fail-open.
- CEL-isms diverge under JS semantics: `has(record.x)`, `in`, `"a" in list`, single-quoted strings inside `${}` templating, `==` coercion (JS `==` is loose where CEL is typed), `size()`, `matches()`, `isBlank()` — none behave per the authoring contract that `validateExpression` / the server enforce.
- Consequence class: an action `visible` predicate that the **server-side** ActionEngine (fail-closed, CEL) and build-time lint both accept can evaluate differently — or not at all — in the browser. The framework's whole guardrail program (ADR-0032, #1928 family, framework#3183) stops at this boundary.

## Why now

framework#3205 just fixed `record.due_date == today()` at the single `celEngine.evaluate` chokepoint. Path A inherits that fix with a dependency bump (objectui#<bump-PR>). **Path B inherits nothing** — it isn't downstream of the engine.

## Proposed direction

Converge Path B onto the canonical engine, exactly as `fieldRules.ts` already does:

1. In `useCondition` / `SchemaRenderer` / `ExpressionProvider`, when the predicate is a `{ dialect: 'cel' }` envelope (or once spec normalizes these sites to CEL), route it to `@objectstack/formula`'s `ExpressionEngine.evaluate` with `{ record, extra: scope }` — same fail-open fallback semantics as today.
2. Keep the legacy `${...}` JS-template path for plain strings during a deprecation window (it's a documented ObjectUI DX shorthand), but stop treating CEL envelopes as JS.
3. Reuse `evalFieldPredicate`'s pattern (or extract a shared `evalCelPredicate`) so there is one client-side delegation point.
4. Bundle-size note: `app-shell`'s `celAuthoring.ts` already lazy-loads `@objectstack/formula` via dynamic `import()` — the same trick applies if engine weight in the base renderer is a concern.

## Acceptance

- [ ] An action `visible: { dialect: 'cel', source: 'record.status == "open" && record.due_date == today()' }` evaluates identically in the browser and in the server ActionEngine (incl. the framework#3205 date-equality fix).
- [ ] `has(...)`, `in`, string equality, `isBlank`, `today()`-family all behave per the CEL catalog in component/action predicates.
- [ ] Legacy `${...}` string predicates unchanged.
- [ ] fieldRules Path A untouched (already canonical).

Refs: framework ADR-0032, framework#1928, framework#3183, framework#3205; `packages/core/src/evaluator/fieldRules.ts` (the in-repo precedent).
